Find applicable evidence-backed ways to reduce execution time in this GitHub Actions workflow. Consider its jobs, dependencies, commands, triggers, and repository manifests.
# Prune the GHCR container caches so they do not grow without bound. All packages are pure caches that are rebuilt on demand, so
# deleting an entry only costs a one-time rebuild on the next run that needs it. Anything meant to persist lives in a separate
# package, so everything in these can be treated as disposable.
#
# The test and doc packages hold base image caches, keyed by a hash of the generated Dockerfile. When a Dockerfile changes a new
# hash tag is pushed and the old tag is orphaned but never overwritten, so stale entries accumulate as tagged images that a rule
# limited to untagged versions can never reach. A cache hit does not re-push, so an entry that is still valid but unchanged ages
# out on its original date. The test-ccache package holds the compile cache, tagged per architecture and overwritten on every
# save, so each save orphans the previous digest as an untagged image with nothing referencing it. The two kinds therefore need
# different rules: age out old tags for test and doc, and simply drop the untagged orphans for test-ccache.
name: ghcr-prune

on:
  schedule:
    # Weekly, on a day and time that does not collide with lock-thread.
    - cron: '30 8 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry-run:
        description: Log what would be deleted without deleting anything
        type: boolean
        default: false

# Deleting package versions requires write access to packages. The default GITHUB_TOKEN works because this repository has the Admin
# role on these packages (it published them). If that ever changes, replace secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN below with a classic PAT that has
# the write:packages and delete:packages scopes.
permissions:
  packages: write

# Never let two prunes run at once.
concurrency:
  group: ghcr-prune

jobs:
  prune:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # The action hardcodes an identical "GHCR Cleanup Summary" heading for every run, so precede each with a heading of our own to
      # label which package the summary below it covers.
      - name: Label test prune
        run: echo '# test (base image cache)' >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY?}"

      # Base image cache. The whole package is disposable, so delete every tag and any untagged manifest older than two months;
      # anything still in use is simply rebuilt and re-pushed on the next run that needs it.
      - name: Prune test base image cache
        uses: dataaxiom/ghcr-cleanup-action@v1
        with:
          package: test
          older-than: 2 months
          delete-tags: '*'
          delete-untagged: true
          dry-run: ${{inputs.dry-run || false}}

      - name: Label doc prune
        run: echo '# doc (base image cache)' >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY?}"

      # Documentation base image cache. Same idea as the test package -- keyed by Dockerfile hash, cache hits do not re-push -- so
      # delete every tag and any untagged manifest older than two months; anything still in use is rebuilt and re-pushed on the next
      # run that needs it.
      - name: Prune doc base image cache
        uses: dataaxiom/ghcr-cleanup-action@v1
        with:
          package: doc
          older-than: 2 months
          delete-tags: '*'
          delete-untagged: true
          dry-run: ${{inputs.dry-run || false}}

      - name: Label test-ccache prune
        run: echo '# test-ccache (compile cache)' >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY?}"

results.content:
Cancel superseded runs

Pattern: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (stale_run_cancellation)

When is cancel superseded runs applicable?

Assess cancel superseded runs for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR; A newer revision supersedes older checks

Contraindications: Release or deployment work; Distinct branches share a cancellation group

Method: Partition cancellation by workflow and branch/PR; Preserve run identity and audit records

Reported finding: Superseding runs can reduce duplicate work.

Reported metrics: {"vm_time_reduction_percent": {"free": 1.9, "paid": 4.1}}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.2.3; Table 4; PDF pp. 7: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf

results.content:
Cache dependency downloads

Pattern: P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency_cache)

When is cache dependency downloads applicable?

Assess cache dependency downloads for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Repeated dependency fetching is measurable; Cache inputs include lockfile and environment

Contraindications: Mutable or untrusted cached content; An equivalent cache already exists

Method: Choose dependency download state rather than unchecked build outputs; Keep installation and all required tests

Reported finding: Caching has modest aggregate benefit.

Reported metrics: {"vm_time_reduction_percent": {"free": 6, "paid": 3.4}}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.2.1; Table 4; PDF pp. 6, 7: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf

Literature example before:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
download dependencies
install dependencies
run required checks


Literature example after:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
restore dependency downloads by lockfile and environment
install dependencies
run required checks


Literature example diff:

--- knowledge/examples/P-LIT-GHA-CACHE/before.txt
+++ knowledge/examples/P-LIT-GHA-CACHE/after.txt
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
 # ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
-download dependencies
+restore dependency downloads by lockfile and environment
 install dependencies
 run required checks
